newsitem.title: GERMANY: Iran warns German court not to condemn Iran.
newsitem.headline: Iran warns German court not to condemn Iran.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati warned on Monday there would be negative repercussions for Germany if a Berlin court condemned the Iranian government for involvement in the murder of Kurdish dissidents.

In an interview with the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung newspaper, Velayati said the possible prosecution of the Iranian government by a state court in another country "would be a first in modern history".

He said both Germany and Iran "could run into an endless dispute...if both countries do not (act) intelligently", and suggested Iranian courts could start holding Germany liable for supplying Iraq with materials used for chemical weapons.
A Berlin state court is trying five men suspected of carrying out political assassinations in Berlin in 1992.

It has spent almost three years hearing evidence in the case of four Lebanese and an Iranian charged with shooting dead three exiled Iranian Kurdish leaders and their translator in a Berlin restaurant known as Mykonos.
The Paris-based National Council of Iran said in a statement released on Monday that it "strongly condems any interference and meddling in the due process of law in the Mykonos trial".
It also urged Germany to abandon its policy of "critical dialogue" with Iran and reject Iran's "shameless demands and disgusting threats".

Last month Iran was angered again when ex-president Abolhassan Banisadr, an enemy of Tehran since fleeing in 1981, said religious leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei ordered the killings and President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani signed the order. Iran denies all involvement in the killings.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said recently he was studying the court testimony to see if there was evidence that Iran ordered the murders.
Velayati said the charges were "one-sided" and "propaganda spread by the Zionist lobby in Germany".
"Certainly, a condemnation of Iran would be more than just another court judgment," he said. "They would be prosecuting the Islamic Republic of Iran in abstenia.

"What value would such a verdict have? If they want to tell the Iranian government something, they should do it at official government level and not allow an ordinary court in one country to condemn the government of another country," Velayati said.
He said Germany could be charged by Iranian courts for the role German firms played in supplying Iraq with the materials used to make chemical weapons.
"Germany helped Baghdad with the development of chemical war materials," Velayati said. "Thousands of Iranians are still suffering from the after effects."
